title: Basic 10 · Apply a filter
summary: Frequency-domain filter (low-pass / high-pass variants) with a tunable cutoff. Previews the live filter response ring.

steps.title: Try a filter
steps.body: Apply a Gaussian low-pass in frequency space to attenuate high-frequency content. We use the **Siemens star** — a radial test chart whose lines become higher-frequency as they approach the centre — so you can see exactly which frequencies the filter cuts.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Siemens Star** onto the canvas.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.siemens` shows the full-frequency star before filtering.

steps.title: Drop the Low-pass node
steps.body: From the Filter category, drag **Filter · Low-pass** (`filter.lp`) next to the Siemens star. The default `kind` is `gauss` — acts as a Gaussian LP out of the box.

steps.title: Wire Siemens → Low-pass
steps.body: Drag from the Siemens Star's right output to the Low-pass's left input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The default cutoff is already mild — the filtered star shows subtle blurring at the centre as a baseline.

steps.title: Click the Low-pass node
steps.body: Click Low-pass. Core params: `kind` (filter shape, default gauss) and `fc` (cutoff in cycles/pixel; 0.5 = Nyquist). Default `fc` is 0.1 (= 10-pixel period). The Inspector shows a live frequency-response plot that updates as you tweak `fc`.

steps.title: Lower fc to 0.05
steps.body: Enter **0.05** in `fc`. The low-pass becomes more aggressive (heavier smoothing).

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The Low-pass node preview shows a smoothed Siemens star — the thin lines near the centre (high frequency) are gone while the thicker outer lines survive: direct visual evidence of what frequencies got cut.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: Drop `fc` to 0.02 and the centre becomes almost a flat disk; raise it to 0.2 and the result is nearly the original. Switch `kind` to `tophat` / `fermi` / `butter` / `raised_cos` to see how the transition shape near the cutoff changes (Comparison 2 explores this in depth).
